definitions.explanation: The emphatic or formal pronunciation of Japan. Used in official contexts, sports cheering, and certain compound words.

examples.japanese: ⟦がんばれ→頑張る：01222_ganbaru⟧、{日本|にっぽん}！
examples.notes: [Note: Common cheer at international sports events]

examples.japanese: ⟦{日本銀行|にっぽんぎんこう}→日本銀行：10141_nipponginkou⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{日本|にほん}→日本：03876_nihon⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{中央銀行|ちゅうおうぎんこう}→中央銀行：10173_chuuouginkou⟧⟦です→です：09485_desu⟧。
examples.english: The Bank of Japan is Japan's central bank.
examples.notes: [Note: 日本銀行 officially uses the にっぽん reading]

examples.japanese: ⟦{日本一|にっぽんいち}→日本一：noentry⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦ラーメン→ラーメン：noentry⟧⟦だ→だ：09496_da⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{言|い}われている→言う：00515_iu⟧。
examples.english: It's said to be the best ramen in Japan.
examples.notes: [Note: 日本一 (number one in Japan) often uses にっぽん]

examples.japanese: ⟦オリンピック→オリンピック：09899_orinpikku⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{日本|にっぽん}⟦{代表|だいひょう}→代表：03419_daihyou⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{金|きん}→金：02666_kin⟧⟦メダル→メダル：10162_medaru⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{取|と}った→取る：00565_toru⟧⟦とき→とき：10077_toki⟧、⟦{会場|かいじょう}→会場：01269_kaijou⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧「{日本|にっぽん}！」⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{声援|せいえん}→声援：10153_seien⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{響|ひび}いた→響く：00099_hibiku⟧。
examples.english: When the Japanese national team won the gold medal at the Olympics, cheers of 'Nippon!' echoed through the venue.

examples.japanese: ⟦{紙幣|しへい}→紙幣：00363_shihei⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧「⟦{日本銀行券|にっぽんぎんこうけん}→日本銀行券：noentry⟧」⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{書|か}いてあり→書く：00477_kaku⟧、⟦{日本|にほん}→日本：03876_nihon⟧⟦ではなく→ではなく：noentry⟧{日本|にっぽん}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{読|よ}む→読む：00426_yomu⟧。
examples.english: Paper money says 'Nippon Ginkō Ken' (Bank of Japan note), read as 'Nippon', not 'Nihon'.

notes:
READING: 日本 has two readings:
・にほん - common, everyday reading
・にっぽん - emphatic, formal, traditional reading

Both readings are officially correct. There is no legal standard.

USES OF にっぽん:
・Sports cheering and patriotic contexts
・Official names: {日本銀行|にっぽんぎんこう} (Bank of Japan), {日本放送協会|にっぽんほうそうきょうかい} (NHK)
・Currency: {日本円|にっぽんえん} on banknotes
・Expressions: {日本一|にっぽんいち} (number one in Japan)
・Stamps and official seals

NOTE: On Japanese currency, にっぽん is used. The passport uses both depending on the edition.

ETYMOLOGY: From {日|ひ}の{本|もと} (origin of the sun), referring to Japan's position east of China.
